title: Amplifiers, oscillators and digital logic
blurb: Explain amplifier classes and efficiency, how oscillators and neutralizing work, and what basic logic circuits do.

G7B01.why: Internal capacitance leaks output back to the input and can make a stage oscillate. Neutralizing cancels that feedback and **eliminates self-oscillation**.
G7B01.trap: Modulation limiting and keying are unrelated to feedback inside a stage.

G7B02.why: The less of the cycle the device conducts, the less power it wastes. Class C conducts least, so it has the **highest efficiency**.
G7B02.trap: Class A is the most linear, not the most efficient.

G7B03.why: An AND gate is high **only when both inputs are high**. Every other input combination gives a low.
G7B03.trap: The other choices describe NAND and NOR behaviour.

G7B04.why: Class A conducts through the entire cycle: **100%**, or 360°.
G7B04.trap: Half the cycle is Class B; less than half is Class C.

G7B05.why: Each bit doubles the states: 2 × 2 × 2 = 2³ = **8** (000 to 111).
G7B05.trap: 16 states needs 4 bits. States grow as a power of 2, not as the bit count.

G7B06.why: A shift register is a **clocked array of circuits**. Each clock pulse moves the data one step along the array.
G7B06.trap: Mixers combine two signals. A shift register does not.

G7B07.why: A sine wave oscillator is an **amplifier plus a filter in a feedback loop**. The filter picks the frequency.
G7B07.trap: Dividers, multipliers and mixers change frequency but do not make a signal sustain itself.

G7B08.why: Efficiency = useful output ÷ power paid for = **RF output ÷ DC input**.
G7B08.trap: Inverted fractions give more than 100%, which is impossible.

G7B09.why: The LC tank is the filter in the loop. Its **inductance and capacitance** set the frequency.
G7B09.trap: Counter and divider stages belong to digital circuits, not LC tanks.

G7B10.why: A linear amplifier's **output preserves the input waveform**, only larger.
G7B10.trap: Linear describes waveform fidelity, not power level or Class C efficiency.

G7B11.why: FM has constant amplitude, so Class C distortion of amplitude does not matter. AM and SSB carry information in amplitude and need a linear stage.
G7B11.trap: SSB and AM both need the output to follow the input amplitude.
